title: Dyadic height gaps isolate the off-diagonal relation points
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $T$ be a Hausdorff topological space, $V$ a topological space, $q:T\to V$ a continuous map, and $H:T\to\mathbb R$ a continuous function. Suppose $(v_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ are distinct points of $V$ and $t_k^-,t_k^+\in T$ satisfy $q^{-1}(\{v_k\})=\{t_k^-,t_k^+\}$ and
$$H(t_k^+)-H(t_k^-)=2^{-k-2}.$$
Assume every fibre over a point outside $\{v_k:k\in\mathbb N\}$ has at most one point. Give $R=\{(x,y)\in T^2:q(x)=q(y)\}$ the subspace topology. Then for every $k$, both singletons $\{(t_k^-,t_k^+)\}$ and $\{(t_k^+,t_k^-)\}$ are open and closed in $R$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-formulated pure-topology auxiliary, old proof Step 5: exact dyadic height-gap isolation in the relation space. No theorem in the blueprint asserts this fact; external reference WANTED.

proof.text: Put $a_j=2^{-j-2}>0$. The height identity implies $t_j^-\ne t_j^+$. If $(x,y)\in R$ and $x\ne y$, their common image cannot lie outside $\{v_j:j\in\mathbb N\}$, since such a fibre has at most one point. Thus it equals some $v_j$, and the exact two-point fibre forces $(x,y)=(t_j^-,t_j^+)$ or $(t_j^+,t_j^-)$. Their height differences $H(y)-H(x)$ are respectively $a_j$ and $-a_j$; diagonal pairs have difference zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; direct elementary proof, Step 1

proof.text: Fix $k$ and put $a=a_k$. For $j>k$, write $j=k+r$ with $r\ge1$; then $a_j=a/2^r\le a/2$. For $j<k$, write $k=j+r$ with $r\ge1$; then $a_j=2^ra\ge2a$. Here $2^r\ge2$ follows by induction from $2^1=2$ and multiplication by $2$. Consequently the interval $(3a/4,5a/4)$ contains $a_k$ and none of $0$, the negative $-a_j$, or the positive $a_j$ for $j\ne k$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; direct elementary proof, Step 2

proof.text: Define $U^-=H^{-1}((H(t_k^-)-a/8,H(t_k^-)+a/8))$ and $U^+=H^{-1}((H(t_k^+)-a/8,H(t_k^+)+a/8))$. These are open by continuity of $H$, and contain $t_k^-$ and $t_k^+$ respectively. The product topology and the definition of the subspace topology make $W^-=R\cap(U^-\times U^+)$ and $W^+=R\cap(U^+\times U^-)$ open in $R$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; direct elementary proof, Step 3

proof.text: For $(x,y)\in W^-$, write $H(x)=H(t_k^-)+e$ and $H(y)=H(t_k^+)+f$, with $|e|,|f|<a/8$. Then $H(y)-H(x)=a+f-e\in(3a/4,5a/4)$. Step 1 and Step 2 force $(x,y)=(t_k^-,t_k^+)$. Conversely this pair lies in $R$ by its fibre identity and belongs to $U^-\times U^+$. Hence $W^-=\{(t_k^-,t_k^+)\}$, proving this singleton open in $R$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; direct elementary proof, Step 4

proof.text: For $(x,y)\in W^+$ the same two window inequalities, now with $H(x)=H(t_k^+)+e$ and $H(y)=H(t_k^-)+f$, give $H(x)-H(y)=a+e-f\in(3a/4,5a/4)$. Apply Step 1 to $(y,x)\in R$ and Step 2 to obtain $(y,x)=(t_k^-,t_k^+)$. The reverse pair itself belongs to $W^+$, so $W^+=\{(t_k^+,t_k^-)\}$ is open in $R$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; direct elementary proof, Step 5

proof.text: For either of these pairs $p=(p_1,p_2)\in R$ and any $z=(z_1,z_2)\in R\setminus\{p\}$, choose a coordinate $i$ with $z_i\ne p_i$. Hausdorffness of $T$ gives disjoint open neighbourhoods of $z_i$ and $p_i$. The inverse image of the former under the $i$th coordinate on $T^2$, intersected with $R$, is an open neighbourhood of $z$ excluding $p$. Their union over all $z\ne p$ is exactly $R\setminus\{p\}$, so this complement is open and $\{p\}$ is closed in $R$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated topology auxiliary; direct elementary proof, Step 6
